panels.general_description: Two stacked line charts of platelet count and CRP by day for four cases, with antibiotic and anticoagulant course bars beneath.
panels.detailed_description: Panel A, top left, is labelled "A". It contains two stacked line charts sharing one day axis. The upper chart has a vertical axis titled "PLT(*10⁹/L)" with ticks 0 to 800 in steps of 100; four colored lines (blue, red, green, yellow) with round markers run across it. The lower chart has a vertical axis titled "CRP(mg/dL)" with ticks 0 to 200 in steps of 20 and a horizontal axis labelled "day" with ticks 0 to 28 in steps of 2; the same four colors show an early high peak for one green line (near 180), a red line near 115 to 125 early on that falls, a yellow line with peaks near 70 and near 50, and blue points that stay below about 40. Four purple right-pointing triangles lie near days 2 to 7. Beneath the charts, text blocks are headed "Case" followed without a space by the numerals 1 to 4 and a colon, each followed by "Antibiotic:" with a solid horizontal line and "Anticoagulant:" with a dashed line of the same color; bracketed day ranges are printed at the line ends: (Day 1–12) and (Day 2–15); (Day 1-22) and (Day 2–23); (Day 1–15) and (Day 2–17); (Day 1–17) and (Day 5–21). The lines of the third and fourth case blocks are yellow and green respectively, whereas the legend assigns green to case 3 and yellow to case 4.

visual.general_description: Four box-and-dot plots of TAT, PIC, sTM and t-PAIC by Pretreatment, Postsurgery and Posttreatment for four cases with dashed upper-limit lines.
visual.detailed_description: Four box-and-dot plots arranged in a two-by-two grid, with no panel letters. Each plot has three categories on the horizontal axis, "Pretreatment", "Postsurgery" and "Posttreatment" (rotated labels), a box with whiskers and median line per category, and colored round points overlaid, and a horizontal dashed line across the plot. Top left: vertical axis "TAT (ng/mL)" with ticks 0 to 50 in steps of 10; the dashed line sits near 4. Top right: "PIC (ug/mL)" with ticks 0 to 8 in steps of 2; the dashed line sits just below 1, and one blue point near the top of the Pretreatment column lies far above the others. Bottom left: "sTM (TU/mL)" with ticks 0 to 20 in steps of 5; the dashed line sits near 13. Bottom right: "t-PAIC (ng/mL)" with ticks 0 to 15 in steps of 5; the dashed line sits at 10. Each plot shows four points in the Pretreatment and Posttreatment columns and three points (red, green, yellow, no blue) in the Postsurgery column. A legend at the bottom shows a dashed line labelled "Upper Limit of Normal (ULN)" and colored dots labelled "Case 1" (blue), "Case 2" (red), "Case 3" (green) and "Case 4" (yellow). In the TAT plot every point in the Pretreatment and Postsurgery columns lies above the dashed line, and two Posttreatment points (blue and green) also remain above it while the other two lie below it.

evidence.quote:
Fig. 2
The levels of TAT, PIC, sTM, and t-PAIC during the hospitalization of four patients. “Pretreatment,” “postsurgery,” and “posttreatment” denote blood samples collected at distinct time points following disease onset: cases 1 (days 1 and 15; this patient did not undergo surgery), 2 (days 1, 4, and 24), 3 (days 2, 5, and 18), and 4 (days 4, 6, and 20). Dotted lines indicate the upper limits of normal for each biomarker: TAT < 4.0 ng/mL, PIC < 0.8 μg/mL, t-PAIC < 10.0 ng/mL, and sTM < 13.3 TU/mL. TAT, thrombin–antithrombin III complex; PIC, plasmin-α2-plasmin inhibitor complex; sTM, soluble thrombomodulin; t-PAIC, tissue plasminogen activator–inhibitor complex; ULN, upper limit of normal.
